name: Service Map
note: Traffic is pushed through a tiered dependency graph by per-edge fan-out factors, so every service's request rate is the sum of its incoming edges and every edge's error rate is what its target returns; the SVG map, sortable table and inspector all read that one model. Rings show each service against its limit, CSS dash animations carry the flow, :has() dims everything outside the hovered path, and --dbo-topology-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Error Budget & Burn-Rate Alerts
note: Thirty-two days of 5-minute good/bad event buckets per objective, kept as prefix sums, so the burn-down, the log-scale hourly burn bars and the SRE-workbook multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerts (1 h & 5 m at 14.4x, 6 h & 30 m at 6x, 3 d & 6 h at 1x) are all exact window subtractions. A what-if switch replays last week's traffic forward to project an outage, its spend and when each alert would fire, and --dbo-budget-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Incident Command Console
note: A phase state machine (investigating to resolved) drives everything: each step logs to the timeline, retunes the console's signal colour by transitioning a registered --dbo-incident-hue, steers the live 5-second impact series toward recovery and finally freezes the clock as time-to-resolve. Severity menu, paging, tasks, timeline composer and status-page templates all write back to the same log; --dbo-incident-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Live Log Explorer
note: A small query language (level:>=warn, svc:, numeric field:>500, quoted phrases, -negation, optional regex) filters a 16k-line live buffer that is drawn as a virtualised list of absolutely positioned 24px rows, with matches highlighted, faceted counts that exclude their own facet, and a DPR-aware canvas histogram stacked by level that you brush to pin a time window. A sticky progress bar runs on animation-timeline: scroll() inside the list's own scroller, and --dbo-logs-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Cluster Capacity & Scheduling
note: Each node is a squarified treemap of its pods' CPU or memory requests against allocatable capacity, and Drain, Uncordon and Add node run a small scheduler (cordon, taints, node selectors, free CPU and memory, least-allocated scoring) whose unschedulable pods land in a Pending tray with the scheduler's own FailedScheduling text. Every move is a cross-parent FLIP via the Web Animations API; --dbo-cluster-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: CI Pipeline Critical Path
note: Sixty seeded runs of a 16-job DAG are scheduled with a forward pass (start = latest dependency end + queue wait), the critical path is walked back from the last job to finish and slack comes from a backward pass; the graph and the Gantt both show it. Mark jobs as simulated cache hits (click, or press C) and the schedule, total and critical path are recomputed, often moving the path to another branch, while the newest run keeps executing in real time; --dbo-pipeline-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Canary Analysis Judge
note: Per-minute baseline and canary samples are judged at each stage boundary with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (tie-corrected normal approximation) over a trailing 10-minute window; a metric fails only when the difference is significant and beyond its tolerance, weighted passes form the score, and a failing critical metric zeroes it. The rollout is simulated forward from those verdicts, so dragging the playhead or replaying at x120 shows exactly what the judge saw (the gauge number is a CSS counter on a registered <integer> property), and --dbo-canary-h can be set to 100dvh in an app.
